title: Duchy of Courland
capsule: The Duchy of Courland and Semigallia was a Baltic duchy established in 1561 when the last master of the Livonian Order, Gotthard Kettler, converted to Lutheranism and accepted the duchy as a fief of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Under Duke Jacob Kettler (1642–1682) the duchy reached its apogee, operating a merchant fleet, exporting timber, iron, and cloth across Europe, and establishing colonies on the Gambia River (1651) and on Tobago (1652). Ernst Johann von Biron, a favourite of Empress Anna of Russia, held the duchy with Russian backing from 1737; his son Peter von Biron relinquished his rights in 1795, and the duchy was absorbed into the Russian Empire through the Third Partition of Poland.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's borders within the Baltic region are well documented through Polish–Lithuanian and later Russian administrative records; the attestation window 1734–1794 corresponds to the Biron period and is amply covered in German, Latvian, and Russian archives.
